findings.title: gate_or_skip's printed signature omits the type the method actually declares
findings.description: RULE.DOC.SIGNATURE_MIRROR requires that an argument typed in the method is typed in the docstring's signature line. The method types `what::AbstractString`, but the docstring's code-block signature shows bare `what`. The sibling docstring in the same file (`check(verb::AbstractString, code::Integer)`, line 14) gets this right, showing the mismatch is a slip rather than a house convention.

findings.title: "the closure gate" (a listed term of art) is named but not linked or explained at first use
locations: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:24 — "Runs the closure gate over the two docs instruments and says whether the build is skipped"
findings.description: `gate` is one of this lane's flagged terms of art and is a documented public binding (`GBGCodingTools.gate`, src/CLI/Gate.jl:26). `gate_or_skip`'s docstring is the first and only place this file names "the closure gate", and it neither `@ref`-links to `GBGCodingTools.gate` nor states in a clause what the gate itself checks (only what happens to its return code). A cold read (module context withheld, per RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED) leaves "the closure gate" as an unexplained term the reader must already know.

findings.title: Comment cites RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND for a mechanism the rule's text does not describe
locations: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:50 — "A round of a docs instrument freezes the build (`RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND`)."
findings.description: RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND (rendered policy, instruments.md) states: "An instrument is never changed mid-round... A change the round wanted and could not make is written one line per deferral in the round's `deferred.md`, and `gbg round close` carries each into `.claude/WORK_QUEUE.md`". That is about not editing an instrument's own code/catalogue while a round using it is open — it says nothing about a docs build skipping while a round is open. The only other citation of this rule id in the codebase, src/CLI/Passes.jl:884 ("Carries a round's deferrals into the session work queue"), matches the rule's actual text; this one does not.

findings.title: "refuses only because a round... is open" is not what the code actually checks
locations: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:25 — "the gate refuses only because a round of a docs instrument is open and `GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP` is unset"
findings.description: `docs_build_skipped` (src/DocLints.jl:44) treats any `code == 1` together with a nonempty `frozen_rounds(cfg, "check-docs", "check-consistency")` as skippable; it never checks that an open docs-instrument round is the sole source of the refusal. `gate()` (src/CLI/Gate.jl:26) can return 1 for an unrelated reason that is independently true at the same time — e.g. an open round of a disabled instrument, added regardless of `wanted` and regardless of `CI` — while a check-docs/check-consistency round also happens to be open. In that concurrent case `gate_or_skip` prints the benign SKIPPED message and returns `true`, silently absorbing the unrelated disabled-instrument refusal into what reads as a routine, expected skip.
